moments.title: A hall built in a hurry
moments.text: Chicago business leaders put up a two-story pine-plank hall at Lake and Market streets near the river for the Republican National Convention. Temporary political halls like it were called wigwams.

moments.title: Lincoln wins on the third ballot
moments.text: At the convention, held May 16 to 18, New York senator William Seward led the first ballot. Abraham Lincoln gained on the second and won the nomination on the third.

moments.title: Destroyed by fire
moments.text: The Wigwam was later destroyed by fire; accounts date the fire to 1867 or November 1869.

moments.title: A centennial plaque
moments.text: For the 100th anniversary of Lincoln's birth, the Daughters of the American Revolution put up a plaque marking the Wigwam site, with the earlier Sauganash Hotel on its other side.

moments.title: The lost plaque returns
moments.text: The DAR plaque, which had ended up in city storage, was rededicated.

moments.title: Today: an office building at Lake and Wacker
moments.text: An office building stands on the site at Lake St and Wacker Dr. Chicago has hosted more major party conventions than any other city, 26 through 2024.

facts.label: Chicago conventions
facts.note: The most of any city; counts vary slightly by how conventions are tallied.

DAR plaque 1909, rededicated 2017 (CBS). Chicago's 26 conventions through 2024 (NPR, Fox 32). Story confirmed; no changes.
